To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) vignettes are a feasible, valid, and reliable method for measuring quality of care for preventive services; 2) the use of vignettes can reduce the cost of quality measurement by 50% compared to the use of chart abstraction; and 3)vignettes may provide a better measure of the quality of preventive services than the chart abstraction method because they are more sensitive to differences in the quality of care across physicians and across sites.
vignettes can measure and can predict variation in quality of care.
the quality of preventive services provided by physicians was measured and predicted by vignettes, and that vignettes may be a more efficient method for measuring quality of care.

the use of clinical vignettes to measure the quality of care for preventive services.
the use of computer-based vignettes as an alternative to chart abstraction for evaluating the quality of care for preventive services.
the development and validation of an assessment instrument that measures the quality of preventive services provided by general internists to their adult patients.
